This an open letter to Michael A Stackpole, an author whose work I enjoy and who I've come to respect as a fantastic science fiction author.

Mr. Stackpole, I've been following you on Twitter for about a year now and I've noticed that on a few different occasions you've actually made some anti-GamerGate tweets. As a long-time GamerGate supporter, I was kind of disappointed to see you buying into the myth that my friends, subscribers and I are somehow misogynists, harassers and a slew of other things.

I understand that there's a lot of misinformation out there about GamerGate. A lot of clickbait games journalists have seemingly made a career out of demonizing gamers as terrible people and crafting a boogieman narrative about us. It can be difficult to get to the truth with so much info and misinfo floating around. But this myth simply isn't true and has been debunked for over a year through multiple studies, links to which are in the description.

We're not Warlord Zsinj, we're just gamers who care about this industry. We don't hate women and we don't hate diversity, we hate corruption and censorship. We're opposed to political extremists who would make this industry smaller by attacking, threatening and shaming artists and game developers for holding the wrong politics. We believe artists and game developers should be able to create art that they want to create, without fear of outside retaliation.

I'm not asking you to become pro-GamerGate or to apologize for your tweets, Mr. Stackpole. All I'm asking, is that you hear us out. That you just keep an open mind to the possibility that maybe we aren't these horrible people that the media and political extremists have painted us as.

Anyway, thanks for hearing me out. I love your work and am looking forward to starting The Bacta War soon. If you wanted to have an nuanced discussion about GamerGate sometime, hit me up on Twitter or via email. I'd like to hear why you hold your anti-GamerGate views, and if you're interested in hearing more about why we hold the views that we hold, then I'd be happy to explain our side as well. All the best, Netscape.
